The Masterclass Core Thesis: Traditional SE vs. Harness Engineering
Deterministic IT Engineering → Non-Deterministic Agentic AI Control Systems
Part 1
The Harness Stack
Five second-level disciplines under harness engineering
Ontology Before Intent
Name the domain before any node acts

points.title: Ontology first
points.body: Define entities, relationships, and rules. Every later node in the graph inherits that vocabulary. No shared ontology, no safe handoff.

points.title: Intent is a binding, not a wish
points.body: Bind a principal to a goal, object, constraints, and a success test. That binding is what a node is allowed to pursue.

points.title: The harness checks the plan
points.body: Validate planned actions against intent and policy. Model confidence is not authorization.

raw_lines: Part 2
From one loop to a graph
Prompt, context, and loop stay inside one agent
Prompt Engineering
Encode the authorized intent for the model

points.title: Put intent in the instruction
points.body: Turn the authorized goal into instructions: output schema, constraints, and a stop rule. Missing stop rules become unbounded runs.

points.title: Separate trust boundaries
points.body: Trusted instructions stay apart from tickets, retrieval, and user text. Untrusted data is not policy.

points.title: Version prompts as artifacts
points.body: Treat the prompt like code. Version it. Test it. Do not ship an untested instruction change into a live graph.

raw_lines: Context Engineering
Give this node only the evidence it needs

points.title: Select for this decision
points.body: Do not dump the corpus into the window. Each node gets evidence for its job, not the whole conversation.

points.title: Attach provenance and scope
points.body: Every retrieved item needs source, freshness, and access scope. Context without provenance is rumor.

points.title: Policy outranks retrieval
points.body: Resolve conflicts before the model sees them. Written policy beats retrieved content.

raw_lines: Loop Engineering
One agent's observe → plan → act → verify cycle

points.title: Verify every cycle
points.body: A single-agent loop without verification is retry theater. Graph nodes still need this cycle internally.

points.title: Cap the cycle, not the graph
points.body: Limit steps, time, cost, and retries on this node. Do not confuse a node retry budget with a graph-level retry of the whole workflow.

points.title: Stop when this node cannot show progress
points.body: If the node cannot demonstrate progress or safety, stop it and take the exception edge. Do not let it spin.

raw_lines: Graph Engineering
Fan-out only when one loop is not enough

points.title: One job per node
points.body: Plan, implement, review, or remediate. Overlapping roles recreate the single-agent bottleneck. Parallel and conditional graphs still need this isolation.

points.title: Edges are contracts
points.body: Pass typed artifacts and scoped authority. Do not forward the transcript. Sequential, parallel, reviewer, and conditional graphs all fail the same way when the edge is chat.

points.title: Exceptions have an owner
points.body: Route failure to a fallback node or a human. A graph with no exception edge is a sequential retry loop with extra processes.

raw_lines: Part 3
Control at every node and edge
A graph inherits the harness; it does not replace it
Automation
Same start, sandbox, and stop on every node

points.title: Automate the node lifecycle
points.body: The harness starts the node, sandboxes its tools, enforces the allowlist, and stops it. Humans set those boundaries. They do not babysit the happy path.

points.title: Failures stay visible
points.body: Do not hide a failed node behind an invisible retry. Log it, bound it, and keep the action idempotent so a replay cannot double-write.

points.title: Humans approve boundaries
points.body: Policy is a human decision. Execution inside that policy is a harness job, including every node in the graph.

raw_lines: Identity and Intent
Who this node acts for, and what it may touch

points.title: Every node run has a principal
points.body: Principal, task ID, and a short-lived credential. Anonymous node processes are unaccountable processes.

points.title: Scope the credential to this node
points.body: The planner's credential must not implement. The implementer's credential must not merge. Shared god-tokens collapse the graph back into one agent.

points.title: Authorize the tool call, not just the sandbox
points.body: A tool the sandbox allows can still be unauthorized for this node's intent. Check both.

raw_lines: Memory
Persist only governed state, per node and per task

points.title: Write for a named purpose
points.body: Memory is not a dump of the transcript. Write it for a named purpose and a named scope, usually one task or one node.

points.title: Isolate tenants, tasks, and nodes
points.body: Cross-node memory without a contract is a leak. Record provenance and retention on every write.

points.title: Treat poison as an incident
points.body: Persistent memory is an attack surface. Detect, quarantine, and roll back. A poisoned planner memory infects every downstream node.

raw_lines: Observability
Reconstruct the path across nodes

points.title: Trace node, edge, and artifact
points.body: Log which node decided, what it passed, and what it wrote. A graph you cannot reconstruct, you cannot govern.

points.title: Keep forensic evidence for high-risk edges
points.body: Credential use, external writes, and authority transfer need the payload, not a summary.

points.title: Protect the traces
points.body: Minimize, access-control, and retain telemetry on purpose. Node logs contain secrets, PII, and attack material.

raw_lines: Runtime Control
Interrupt a live graph, not only a live loop

points.title: Pause, stop, or re-policy in flight
points.body: Operators must pause one node or the whole graph. A graph that cannot be interrupted is unsupervised execution.

points.title: Checkpoint before irreversible edges
points.body: Snapshot before merge, deploy, or external write. Support rollback of that node without replaying the entire graph.

points.title: No interrupt path, no trustworthy autonomy
points.body: If you cannot stop the implementer, the reviewer never gets a turn that matters.

raw_lines: Evaluation
Gate the graph, not only the prompt

points.title: Score success and boundary compliance
points.body: A graph that finishes while violating a node boundary has failed. Score both.

points.title: Re-evaluate when the graph changes
points.body: A new node, tool, prompt, or model is a release of the graph. Re-run the gate.

points.title: Failed eval drops autonomy
points.body: Block the release or collapse the graph to fewer nodes and tighter credentials. Do not ship a failing topology at full fan-out.

raw_lines: Scalability
Fan-out safety, not only fan-out throughput

points.title: Admit work before spawning nodes
points.body: Admission control and backpressure come first. Unbounded fan-out is a denial-of-service against your own harness.

points.title: Isolate tenants and workers
points.body: Contain a failed or poisoned node. It must not contaminate sibling nodes or other tenants.

points.title: Idempotent replay at fleet scale
points.body: At ten nodes, a double-write is a bug. At ten thousand, it is an incident. Retries must not multiply side effects.

raw_lines: Token Budget
Cap cost and injection surface per node and per graph

points.title: Budget the node and the graph
points.body: Set token and tool-output caps per node and a ceiling for the whole graph. Unbounded context is unbounded spend and unbounded injection.

points.title: Stop at the cap
points.body: Hit the ceiling, stop that node, take the exception edge. Never continue silently past the budget.

points.title: Raising the cap is a policy change
points.body: A bigger window is not a tuning knob. It is a policy change and it requires evaluation of the graph.

raw_lines: Part 4
Tools the graph is allowed to use
Extensions are edges to capability, not free power
Extensions
How a node obtains a tool

points.title: Inventory before the node can call it
points.body: Skills, plugins, MCP servers, hooks, and CLI tools are attack surface. Nothing joins a node without an inventory record and an approval.

points.title: Typed actions, least privilege
points.body: Prefer typed tool calls over shell. Issue credentials scoped to that node. A shared token turns every extension into admin across the graph.

points.title: Validate I/O and revoke
points.body: Check inputs and outputs at the edge. An extension that fails policy is revoked from the graph, not warned.
